claim: Attack rate is a metric taken from Zhan et al. (the Source column of Table 4.5).
quote: For stochastic cyber attack pr ocesses, the primary statistic is the attack rate , which describes the number of attacks that arrive at unit time (e.g., min ute or hour or day).
locator: p. 1778 printed (PDF p. 4), Sec. III-B Step 2
issue: Zhan's attack rate counts attacks (honeypot TCP flows, from many attackers) arriving at a victim, port or network per unit time, a defender-side arrival count; the dissertation's metric counts one attacker's own attack actions per minute. The name and form are borrowed, the instantiation is ours.
fix_text: Source cell "\citep{zhan2013}" -> "this dissertation, after \citep{zhan2013}" (the form the table already uses for Distinct openings after hong2018).

claim: Attack rate is the number of attack actions an attacker takes per minute (as Zhan et al. define it).
quote: For stochastic cyber attack pr ocesses, the primary statistic is the attack rate , which describes the number of attacks that arrive at unit time (e.g., min ute or hour or day). Note that attack rate can be instantiated at various resolutions of attack processes, such as: network-level attack rate, victim-level attack rate and port-level attack rate.
locator: p. 1778 printed (PDF p. 4), Sec. III-B Step 2; the case study uses per hour, p. 1779 printed (PDF p. 5), Sec. IV-B
issue: Zhan defines attack rate as attacks arriving at a target per unit time (minute is one example unit; the case study uses per hour), observed by the defender across many attackers; it is not the attack actions one attacker takes. Even Zhan's attacker-level process keeps only each attacker's first attack against a victim.
fix_text: "Attack rate is the number of attack actions an attacker takes per minute \citep{zhan2013}" -> "Attack rate, after the number of attacks per unit time of \citet{zhan2013}, is the number of attack actions an attacker takes per minute" (or "adapting \citep{zhan2013}").
